stem: Vikram starts at point O facing North. He walks 4 km, then turns left and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 2 km. In which direction is Vikram from point O now?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Facing North, turn left (West), walk 3 km, turn right (North), walk 2 km: final position is 3 km West and 6 km North of O, which is North-West.
Swapping left for right and right for left at every turn places Vikram 3 km East and 6 km North of O, which is North-East.
Adding all distances as a straight northward journey (4+3+2 = 9 km North) and ignoring the direction changes gives a final position due North.
Reading the starting direction as South instead of North places Vikram 3 km East and 6 km South of O, which is South-East.

explanation: From O, Vikram walks 4 km North to (0,4). He turns left (now facing West) and walks 3 km to (-3,4). He turns right (now facing North again) and walks 2 km to (-3,6). Relative to O, he is 3 km West and 6 km North, placing him in the North-West direction.

explanation_sections.punchline: Lock each facing direction before moving: North, then left turn gives West, then right turn gives North again. Final coordinates are (-3, 6), which is North-West of O.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues in order of movement. Set O at (0,0) and note initial facing: North. Segment 1: walk 4 km North to (0,4). Turn 1: left from North = now facing West. Segment 2: walk 3 km West to (-3,4). Turn 2: right from West = now facing North. Segment 3: walk 2 km North to (-3,6). Read the quadrant from the final sign: negative x is West, positive y is North, so the direction from O is North-West. Verify by re-reading each instruction against your diagram.
explanation_sections.lesson: After every turn, update the facing direction before computing the next displacement. The compass turn is the most common error point, not the arithmetic.
explanation_sections.timing: About 75 seconds. Two turns and three segments. Spend 10 seconds per segment; the critical check is after the left turn at step 2. Option North-East is the mirror trap: it comes from swapping left and right throughout.
